findings.title: $__range check now runs on already-interpolated expressions, so range queries get split
findings.body: Queries are now interpolated at the top of runSplitQuery, before querySupportsSplitting() runs at line 300. querySupportsSplitting() relies on isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) to keep $__range queries out of splitting, and its comment says the $__range variable must not be split because it is computed for the full time range. Once $__range has been replaced with a concrete duration, the check no longer matches, so such queries are split and each sub-request gets an incorrect $__range value. The range-variable check should run on the original expression, or the query should be classified before interpolation.

findings.title: Queries are interpolated twice on the sharded path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls applyTemplateVariables on every target, and the result is passed to splitQueriesByStreamShard. That code then calls runSplitQuery for each subRequest, and runSplitQuery calls applyTemplateVariables again on the same targets. Values that contain `$` or other template syntax can be expanded a second time, and the interpolation is not idempotent in general. Interpolation should happen in one place only.

findings.title: Assertion pins the exact applyTemplateVariables call count
findings.body: The test expects applyTemplateVariables to be called exactly 5 times. That count depends on how many shard groups and sub-requests the implementation creates, and it will break on unrelated refactors while not checking that interpolation happens before execution. The test should assert on the interpolated expressions passed to runQuery instead.
